output.brief: Do not roll back gateway 5.8. The regression is almost certainly caused by the 2 Nov compaction tuning change on storage nodes, not by the gateway. Per-cell data shows every cell with that change jumped to about 300 ms within minutes of the push, including cells still running 5.7 at the time. The one cell that skipped the change (aps-3) took 5.8 and stayed at about 94 ms. Rolling euw-1 back to 5.7 changed nothing. After the change, storage disks went from 41% to 97% busy and node-side read time rose from 61 to 262 ms. Network and traffic growth don't explain it, since aps-3 saw the same traffic growth. A rollback would waste about 4 hours, leave the security flaw open, and not fix latency. Next step: revert the tuning in one cell, watch GET p99 and compaction backlog, then extend to the rest. Do not pause compaction, because backlog would build up and risk full disks. The backlog is currently about 4%, well under the 15% danger level, so Orrin rate-limiting can wait for the 10 Nov attribution report. Unknown: what actually drove the earlier backlog growth (Orrin or the cold-tier expiry sweep). Confidence is high on the main cause.
